justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift across the three horizons, starting near 338.5 for the one-day forecast and gradually rising to 343 at one month. This gentle positive slope is consistent with a baseline assumption of slow, mean-reverting growth in whatever underlying series this represents, likely a macro or financial indicator trading near recent levels. The one-day estimate is anchored heavily by the most recent observed value, with only minor drift expected over such a short window. The one-week and one-month estimates incorporate slightly more trend momentum, suggesting the series has been in a mild uptrend, but I have not assumed any sharp acceleration or reversal in the absence of a specific catalyst.

The confidence interval widths expand meaningfully as the horizon lengthens, which reflects the standard compounding of uncertainty over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 15 points, reflecting relatively tight short-run volatility. By one week, that expands to about 28 points, and at one month it reaches 56 points. This scaling is roughly consistent with a random-walk-style uncertainty structure where variance grows approximately with the square root of time. The width at each horizon also reflects uncertainty about whether recent momentum will persist, fade, or reverse, which becomes a larger factor over longer windows.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these intervals. On the upside, a positive macro surprise, a shift in sentiment, or a policy announcement supportive of the underlying could push the series above 371 at the one-month horizon. On the downside, a risk-off episode, disappointing data releases, or broader market stress could push values below 315. There is also model uncertainty to acknowledge: if the series has recently undergone a structural shift or if volatility has been unusually low relative to its historical norm, my intervals may be systematically too narrow. Tail events, by their nature, are underweighted in point-estimate-centric frameworks, so the true probability of extreme outcomes may be somewhat higher than the stated 10% outside my bounds.
